hero_headline: Bank of England hikes to 4% as Democrats take Congress and Big Tech buybacks hit a seven-year low
daily_overview: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate a quarter point to 4%, its first increase in more than three years, and warned inflation is tracking toward almost 5% next year while flagging another hike. US markets read the midterm result as a split signal: Democrats regained Congress, yet equity desks are still pitching a year-end rally, and the Economist reports investors largely yawned at the outcome. The more concrete corporate signal is capital allocation. Combined buybacks at Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle fell to $4.4 billion in Q3 2026, the lowest since Q3 2017 and roughly 90% below the $45.9 billion peak, as cash rotates into AI infrastructure. That buildout is now political: Texas, the fastest-growing US data center market, may lose its edge after Democrats swept the state. On the technology side, OpenAI disclosed an autonomous pipeline that found, validated and patched 948 Linux kernel privilege-escalation vulnerabilities, and agreed to acquire Pierre Computer Company to expand Codex tooling. In Europe, Rheinmetall cut guidance and fell 17% on a Boxer order delay, China planned its first yuan sovereign bond sale in Canada, and a coordinated wave of bomb threats diverted flights across the continent.

tech_briefs.title: OpenAI pipeline finds and patches 948 Linux kernel privilege-escalation flaws
tech_briefs.summary: 948. That is how many local privilege-escalation vulnerabilities OpenAI's autonomous pipeline found, validated and patched in the Linux kernel, roughly a thousand fewer paths to root in a single cycle. The take: patch volume is becoming a function of model throughput, not headcount, and defensive security budgets should be repriced accordingly. Not financial advice. Views are my own.

tech_briefs.title: Big Tech buybacks fall to $4.4 billion in Q3 2026, lowest since 2017
tech_briefs.summary: Big Tech buybacks fell to $4.4 billion in Q3 2026, the lowest since Q3 2017 and about 90% below the $45.9 billion peak, based on combined GOOGL, AMZN, MSFT, META and ORCL disclosures. Mechanism: free cash flow is being redirected into AI data center capex, so the EPS tailwind that buyback desks and index funds leaned on for a decade is shrinking. Treasury and equity capital markets teams should model lower net share reduction into 2027. Not financial advice. Views are my own.

tech_briefs.title: Texas data center buildout faces political risk after state midterm shift
tech_briefs.summary: Texas was the fastest-growing US data center market and the center of the largest AI buildouts. After the blue wave in the state, that pipeline is now a permitting and power-contract question, not a demand question. If you trade utilities, grid names or REITs with Texas exposure, are you hedging the political risk or underwriting it? Full breakdown, link in my bio. Not financial advice. Views are my own.

finance_briefs.title: Bank of England raises Bank Rate to 4% and warns inflation nears 5% next year
finance_briefs.summary: The Bank of England lifted rates a quarter point from 3.75% to 4%, the first increase in over three years and in line with most analyst expectations. Policymakers said inflation is on track to approach 5% next year and signalled another hike is possible. Higher rates feed through to mortgages, loans and savings rates. (multiple reports)

finance_briefs.title: Rheinmetall shares drop 17% after sales forecast cut on Boxer order delay
finance_briefs.summary: Rheinmetall shares fell 17% after the German defence group cut its sales forecast, citing a delay to a Boxer armoured vehicle order. The setback tests the sector's re-rating thesis, which has rested on European rearmament budgets converting into booked revenue. Investors will now watch whether the delay is timing or a broader order-conversion problem.

finance_briefs.title: China plans first yuan-denominated sovereign bond sale in Canada
finance_briefs.summary: China is planning to issue yuan-denominated sovereign bonds in Canada for the first time, as the two countries rebuild bilateral ties after years of diplomatic strain. The deal is small in scale but notable as a template for offshore renminbi distribution outside traditional hubs, and it gives Canadian investors direct sovereign credit exposure denominated in the Chinese currency.

finance_briefs.title: Wall Street desks position for a year-end US equity rally
finance_briefs.summary: Trading desks are arguing the path of least resistance for US stocks is higher into year-end, leaning on positioning and seasonal flows rather than a change in earnings expectations. The case sits alongside a weaker buyback bid and a divided government outcome that the Economist says investors met with little reaction.

politics_briefs.title: Democrats regain control of Congress, plan investigations as some races remain uncalled
politics_briefs.summary: Democrats have won control of Congress and are preparing a slate of investigations into the Trump administration, according to NPR. Several races remain uncalled, and the size of the majority will shape which oversight and legislative items can actually advance. Trump is facing backlash after the result.

politics_briefs.title: Coordinated bomb threats divert commercial flights across Europe
politics_briefs.summary: A new series of bomb threats disrupted commercial aviation across Europe, with flights in Italy, France and elsewhere diverted or delayed. Targeted aircraft landed safely and no explosives were found, officials said. Security experts describe the pattern as a coordinated campaign against regional air travel rather than isolated incidents. (multiple reports)

politics_briefs.title: Netanyahu alleges election fraud over Arab turnout as officials dispute impact
politics_briefs.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his allies are alleging that Arab voters stole last month's election. Election officials said foul play is under investigation but could not have changed the result. The dispute matters for coalition formation and for the durability of policy decisions taken by the current government.

editor_note: This brief separates confirmed disclosures from market narrative. Buyback figures are company-reported and cover five issuers only; BOE guidance is language, not forecast. Texas data center risk stays speculative until permitting and power contracts are renegotiated. European flight disruptions remain unresolved.
